title: Declare C-family primary execution stack, one-language-one-format convergence, and A610 language reallocation
summary: Re-order the governed language stack so C23/C++23/C#14 (.NET 10 GC, unified format, automatic memory management) carry primary execution, bound Python to on-demand governance semantics, declare exactly one canonical authored-source format per language with grandfathered alternates denied for new files, and introduce provision A610 anchoring RULE_LANGUAGE_REALLOCATION_V1. Composes on the executed go-rust r3 text; Go and Rust keep their bounded roles.
origin: human-governor directive 2026-09-25: unify file formats (one language one format), optimize for high performance, high execution speed, low consumption and low resource footprint, reduce Python dependency, C/C++/C# primary on .NET 10; r2 restamp after go-rust r3 execution and RULE_LANGUAGE_REALLOCATION_V1 evaluator registration

problem.summary: The implementation language surface has drifted from the declared stack: TypeScript accumulates .tsx/.d.ts alternates, the C# source roots in policy did not cover the registered .NET tools, process-metrics-csharp had no architecture registration, and the codex does not declare a primary execution order, a single canonical format per language, or a provision anchoring the registered RULE_LANGUAGE_REALLOCATION_V1 evaluator (C23/C++23/C#14 .NET 10 primary adaptive).
problem.codex_state: A35 lists the hybrid stack at c11/c++17 without a primary execution order or .NET 10 GC target; A341 lacks a primary-execution row; A348 lists multi-extension sets per language without primary/grandfathered distinction and omits fsharp from ALLOWED-LANGUAGES although A35 declares it in the stack; A604 assigns language responsibility without the C-family-primary optimization target; no provision anchors RULE_LANGUAGE_REALLOCATION_V1.
problem.risk_if_unamended: Extension alternates proliferate, the boundary gate cannot enforce a single canonical format, F# remains owned-but-disallowed, the reallocation evaluator lacks a codex anchor, and Python keeps absorbing execution work that the optimization target assigns to C/C++/C#.
